subject: Request: uptime carveout for customer-managed gateway (Medisys)
body:
-----Original Message-----
From: Kerry Jenkins <kerry.jenkins@medisys.io>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Medisys Security <security@medisys.io>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Uptime SLA request for customer-managed gateway

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. As discussed, Medisys plans to deploy a customer-managed gateway appliance in our data centers that terminates customer traffic before it reaches Redwood Private instances. Given our operational model, we need to ensure the contract reflects that outages caused by our gateway or our network provider are not counted against Redwood uptime SLA.

Can you:
- Confirm whether Redwood can add a carveout excluding "customer-managed gateway / on-prem network" events from uptime/latency SLA credits;
- Provide suggested contract language we can review with our legal team;
- Share any required evidence/SOC2 artifacts you need from us to qualify for the carveout.

We'd like to get a signed amendment before go-live (target mid-Feb).

Thanks,
Kerry Jenkins
Director, Infrastructure
Medisys Health
kerry.jenkins@medisys.io
(415) 555-0132

-----Reply (Priya Natarajan)-----
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Kerry Jenkins <kerry.jenkins@medisys.io>
Cc: Medisys Security <security@medisys.io>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 13:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Uptime SLA request for customer-managed gateway

Hi Kerry — thanks for the clear notes. We can accommodate a shared-responsibility carveout for customer-controlled network hardware, but we'll need a bit more detail to scope the work and final language. Can you attach:

- A brief network diagram showing the gateway placement (edge vs. inline) and which traffic classes are affected;
- Any maintenance windows your infra team expects to run that would affect connectivity;
- Point-of-contact for on-call coordination.

From Redwood's side, we typically propose:
- Exclusion language that omits "customer-managed network devices and on-prem gateways" from SLA calculations when the root cause is confirmed to be customer-controlled;
- A runbook & escalation path (we propose a 2-hour triage SLA for joint investigations, and best-effort remediation vs SLA credit for customer-side faults);
- Optional hybrid fallback routing to our hosted edge for critical flows (this has cost and design implications).

I've looped in Vivek to confirm technical impacts (KV cache, latency tails) and Monica for contract language and legal coordination. I'll draft suggested amendment language and share.

—Priya
Priya Natarajan
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com

-----Internal: Priya -> Vivek, Monica-----
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jan 2028 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Medisys carveout — recommended language and ops model

Team — forwarding Kerry's ask. Key constraints from product/infra perspective:
- If customer gateway drops packets or produces significant latency, Redwood's hosted-side SLOs should not apply for that specific session, but we need deterministic detection (customer fault vs Redwood).
- Customer-managed KV caches (if they mirror session state) introduce cache-coherency risk and can exacerbate tail latency; we should call that out.

Recommended amendment (working draft, attached):
1) Definitions: 
   - "Customer-Managed Gateway": any appliance, virtual or physical, operated by the Customer that performs ingress/egress termination prior to Redwood Private ingestion.
2) Exclusion: 
   - "Redwood will exclude from SLA calculations any unavailability, latency degradation, or packet loss events where the primary root cause is determined to be the Customer-Managed Gateway, Customer network provider, or Customer-controlled infrastructure.
3) Investigation & Credits: 
   - Joint investigation window: 30 days to complete RCA.
   - During the investigation window Redwood will provide diagnostic logs and packet summaries (as available).
   - If root cause is Redwood, standard credits apply. If root cause is Customer, no SLA credit and Redwood will provide best-effort support per the joint runbook.
4) Optional Mitigations:
   - Hybrid fallback: route critical traffic to Redwood hosted edge with a failover policy for a capped incremental cost.
   - Concierge onboarding review to validate gateway configuration and connectivity.

Attachments: draft_gw_carveout_20280116.docx (working amendment), medisys_network_diagram.png (ask from Kerry).

Questions for you: Vivek — is the hybrid fallback feasible without customer-side code changes? Monica — is the 30-day RCA window and "best-effort" language something legal will accept or push back for credit/calculation mechanics?

—Priya

-----Reply: Vivek Kulkarni (technical notes)-----
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Jan 2028 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Medisys carveout — recommended language and ops model

Quick technical caveats:
- Hybrid fallback is possible but requires session affinity handling; if the gateway terminates TLS and rewrites headers we may need a short-lived token exchange to preserve KV cache semantics. That means a small SDK/workflow change on Medisys side for session pinning if they want zero tail latency.
- For detection: we'll rely on cross-correlation of Redwood ingress logs + customer packet captures (pcap snippets). If customer cannot supply capture due to privacy/regulatory limits, RCA may be inconclusive — recommend adding a clause for "insufficient diagnostic evidence" where investigation outcomes default to "inconclusive" and no credit is issued.
- Suggest adding explicit latency thresholds for exclusion (e.g., "events where median backend latency is > X ms and network loss > Y% as measured by both sides").

I can draft the technical appendix to the amendment.

—Vivek
VP, Serving Runtime
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

-----Final: Priya -> Kerry, CC Vivek, Monica (proposal and next steps)-----
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Kerry Jenkins <kerry.jenkins@medisys.io>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Medisys Legal <contracts@medisys.io>
Date: Fri, 19 Jan 2028 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Uptime SLA request for customer-managed gateway

Kerry — thanks for the quick turn. Attached is a proposed amendment (draft_gw_carveout_20280116.docx) and a short technical appendix (included in the doc) that reflects Vivek's points. Key items:
- Carveout text that excludes confirmed customer-managed gateway/network events from SLA calculation.
- 30-day joint RCA window and "inconclusive" default when diagnostics are insufficient.
- Optional hybrid fallback described with a short bullet on implementation and cost.

Next steps I propose:
1) Medisys reviews the draft and returns comments by Tue 23 Jan.
2) Redwood and Medisys run a 60-minute technical call (we can do Wed 24 Jan) to walk the appendix and any session affinity requirements.
3) We move to DocuSign following legal alignment — preliminary DocuSign envelope: https://docusign.com/ABC123

If this timeline works I'll bring this to contracting for formal redline.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the line.

—Priya
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: draft_gw_carveout_20280116.docx (working amendment), medisys_network_diagram.png (customer diagram)
